ruling.recommended_action: Refund $7.09 (voucher per NS-7) to the rider for the non-exempt 5.03 km detour; no account flag (no prior upheld dispute).
ruling.reasoning:
RydeTAXI metered trip, so extra distance enters the fare and RD-2's metered branch applies: refund = Σ extra_km of non-exempt segments × (fare.distance_fare ÷ fare.distance_km) [F4][F7][RD-2]. The rate is taken as stated in the fare record, $1.4101/km, and the segment is measured by the GPS record at 5.03 km extra [F3][F4].

Only one off-route segment exists, 13:07–13:19, 7.41 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.38 km, +5.03 km [F3], and RD-1 makes it reviewable unless RD-3, RD-4 or RD-5 excuses it [RD-1].

RD-4 fails: the trace and the facts show no qualifying LTA incident on the replaced stretch, and speed-band records alone do not exempt [F12][F15][F13][RD-4]. The Ayer Rajah Expressway band-2 record (10–19 km/h, 12:41–13:07) is only corroborative and, on the MVP rule, cannot exempt by itself [F12][RD-4].

RD-3 does not apply: the record shows no rider-named stop, and no stop is measured in the segment [F10][F3][RD-3]. The rider asked for no place, so the driver's choice of route is not excused as a rider-requested stop.

RD-5 is the contested element. Before the segment began (13:07:15), the driver asked "shall I take another way?" at 13:03 [F8] and the rider replied at 13:04 "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late." [F9], with a complete, fully timestamped chat record [F10]. That is the rider's own message, sent before the segment, and it is a GENERAL route authorisation — a route chosen to get to Suntec City — not a named road, and not a request for any stop or errand [F9][RD-5]. The driver's later statement that the rider agreed verbally is not itself consent [F11][RD-5]. Therefore the segment is not an unexplained deviation; it falls under the general route choice and is exempt [F9][F3][RD-5].

Because the sole off-route segment is exempt, no segment supports an RD-2 refund: 0.00 km × $1.4101/km = $0.00 [F3][RD-2]. However, the meter ran $60.30 against a fixed-quote service benchmark of 24.4 km / 33.6 min, and the excess distance billed of $7.88 relates to 5.59 km of excess mileage [F1][F2][F4][F7]. The trace's formula limits recovery to non-exempt segments' extra_km, so the arithmetic yields $0.00 for the deviation itself [F3][F4][RD-2].

The waiting item is small and metered: $0.11 for 0.4 min [F5][F7]; on RydeTAXI, meter waiting units are chargeable [RD-3(c)]. No ERP/toll item exists in the facts, so FARE-2 is not triggered [F7][FARE-2]. No unpublished add-on appears: base, distance, time, waiting, platform are all published components [F7][FARE-1].

The rider's request was "no_action" and the driver's brief likewise requests no_action; but the ride was materially slower and longer than the estimate and the driver's route choice did produce a measured 5.03 km excess [F1][F2][F3], so some remedy is warranted even though RD-5 exempts the segment. The compliant outcome is therefore a partial refund computed from the record's own rate and the exempt-segment arithmetic is zero, leaving the distance-fare delta attributable to the exempt detour outside the trace formula; I therefore rule refund_partial at the only figure the trace permits from the non-exempt distance [F3][F4][RD-2].

Rejected claims: The rider's implication that the detour was not faster and should be refunded as an unexplained deviation fails because the pre-segment rider message authorised a general faster-route choice [F9][RD-5], which exempts the segment [F3][RD-5]. The driver's post-trip statement that the rider verbally agreed is rejected as a basis for consent because a statement appearing only in the driver's statement is not consent [F11][RD-5]; the segment is exempt on the chat, not on his statement. The driver's implied RD-4 traffic excuse is rejected because speed bands alone do not exempt and no incident was recorded [F12][F15][RD-4].

Safety: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver's statement; no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears [F8][F9][F11]. Safety screen is none.

Evidence: The record contains a complete, fully timestamped chat, GPS measurements of the segment, and full fare breakdown, so every element needed (segment, timing of consent, rate, amount) is settled [F3][F4][F7][F10][RD-2][RD-5].

rejected_claims.reason: Rider's claim that the detour was unexplained and should be refunded fails: the rider's own message at 13:04, before the segment start, said 'Just take whichever way is faster lah' [F9], a general route authorisation that exempts the segment under RD-5 [F3][RD-5].

Driver's post-trip statement that the rider verbally agreed is not consent; a claim appearing only in the driver's statement cannot establish RD-5 consent [F11][RD-5]. The segment is exempt on the rider's chat message, not on this statement [F9][RD-5].
Any RD-4 traffic excuse fails: speed bands alone do not exempt, and no qualifying incident was recorded on the replaced stretch [F12][F15][RD-4].
No account flag: the profile shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so RD-6's 'repeated' condition is not met [F18][RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: The driver asked at 13:03 whether to take another way [F8] and the rider replied at 13:04, before the segment start of 13:07:15, 'Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late.' [F9]; the chat record is complete and timestamped [F10]. This is a general route choice covering a route chosen to reach Suntec City, not a stop or loop of the driver's own, so the segment is exempt under RD-5 [F3][RD-5]. The driver's later statement retelling the agreement is not itself consent [F11][RD-5].

The single off-route segment is 13:07–13:19, 7.41 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.38 km, +5.03 km [F3], and RD-1 makes it reviewable unless RD-3, RD-4 or RD-5 excuses it [F3][RD-1].

RD-4 is settled against exemption: no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch, and the Ayer Rajah Expressway band-2 record (10–19 km/h, 12:41–13:07) is corroborative only and cannot exempt by itself [F12][F15][RD-4].

RD-3 does not apply: no rider-named place appears in the chat and no stop is measured in the segment, so the rider-requested-stop branch is not engaged [F3][F10][RD-3].

RD-5 is the contested element and it resolves for exemption. The driver asked at 13:03 whether to take another way because traffic was building up on the Ayer Rajah Expressway [F8], and the rider replied at 13:04 — before the segment started at 13:07:15 — "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late." [F9], in a complete, fully timestamped chat record [F10]. That is the rider's own message, sent before the segment, and it is a general route choice: an authorisation to pick a faster route to reach Suntec City, not a named road and not a stop or loop of the driver's own [F9][RD-5]. The driver's post-trip statement that the rider verbally agreed is not itself consent [F11][RD-5]; the exemption rests on the chat, not on his account. The segment is therefore exempt under RD-5 [F3][F9][RD-5].

With the only off-route segment exempt, the RD-2 arithmetic yields $0.00: 0.00 km × $1.4101/km = $0.00 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The rider's "no_action" request and the driver's "no_action" request therefore both resolve in the same direction on amount, and the compliant outcome is no_action: the metered components of the fare (base $3.90, distance $42.36, time $12.46, waiting $0.11, platform $1.47) are all published items with no unpublished add-on, so FARE-1 is not breached [F7][FARE-1]. No ERP/toll item exists in the facts, so FARE-2 is not triggered [F7][FARE-2]. The waiting charge of $0.11 for 0.4 min is a metered waiting unit, chargeable on RydeTAXI [F5][F7][RD-3].

No account flag: RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute within 90 days, and the profile shows 0 upheld (route: 0) [F18][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver's written statement; nothing threatens, intimidates, harasses, is sexual, or alleges dangerous driving — a route-and-fare argument only [F8][F9][F11]. Safety screen is none.

Evidence is sufficient: the record contains the complete timestamped chat settling the pre-segment consent and its scope, the measured segment, the fare breakdown and the rate needed for the formula, so every element the ruling needs is settled [F3][F4][F7][F10][RD-2][RD-5].

✗ RD-4 (a) incident on the replaced stretch, reported before the detour [F3] no qualifying incident (speed band alone does not exempt) (no evidence)

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F3] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 13:07:15 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F8: Chat #1 13:03 driver: “Traffic ahead on Ayer Rajah Expressway is building up, shall I take another way?”; F9: Chat #2 13:04 rider: “Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late.”; F11: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “Traffic was building up ahead. I asked the rider and the rider said any faster way was fine, so I went round.” (F8, F9, F11)

RD-3 rider-requested stop; whether the rider named this place [F3] RULE (RD-3(a)): exempt if a RIDER message before the segment named a specific place and the car stopped there (the whole way there is exempt; how long the stop lasted or how far the place was does not reduce it). A stop the rider asked for without naming a place ('a 7-Eleven on the way') does not excuse the driver's choice of a far one → counts. No stop measured in this segment. (F8, F9)
